newsitem.title: USA: Israel, Palestinian security cooperation agreed-US.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinian security cooperation agreed-US.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian officials have agreed to a procedure for restoring security cooperation and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is encouraged by the move, the State Department said on Tuesday.

During three days of talks with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, the two sides revived a means of sharing information and acting together to combat terrorism, spokesman James Rubin said, adding: "Now we're going to be looking for results, results, results."

U.S. officials said the two sides agreed to have intelligence and security experts meet regularly to trade information on extremists and potential attacks. This would reinstate a cooperative relationship that existed previously.
"And so, this is not a breakthrough. But it is encouraging that a mechanism has been found, and now we're going to look for results, results, results," Rubin told a news briefing.
He said Albright and Ross "believe that, procedurally, things are much better today than they were yesterday."
Israelis and Palestinians are deeply mistrustful of each other after a July 30 suicide bombing by Moslem militants of Jerusalem's main Jewish market and Israeli actions against Palestinians.
These include building new Jewish settlements in Arab parts of Jerusalem and withholding VAT and other taxes due the Palestinian Authority.
Rubin said Ross would hold another round of talks in Israel on Wednesday and then fly home to Washington.

No date has been set yet for a trip to the region by Albright, he said. But "to the extent that the discussions over the last 24 hours that we hope to continue today yield results, the trip becomes highly likely," he said.
U.S. officials were looking at an Albright trip for the last week of August but say that may slip into September.

Washington is hopeful that if Palestinians follow through and cooperate in a crackdown against Moslem militants, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will ease sanctions imposed on Palestinians, like withholding the taxes, Rubin said.

He reiterated the U.S. view that while Israel's closing of borders with Palestinian areas is "understandable when a country has gone through the trauma of a terrorist bombing," withholding financial transfers to the Palestinian Authority is punitive, counterproductive and does not encourage security cooperation.

Albright said in a speech last week that in addition to sharing information and coordinating law enforcement actions with Israel, Palestinians must wage an "unrelenting effort to detect and deter potential terrorist acts."

This means seizing arms caches -- like the one raided successfully by Palestinian police in Beit Sahour three weeks ago -- as well as arresting and prosecuting persons involved in planning, fincnaing, supplying or abetting terrorism, she said.
Also, it means Palestinians "must do everything possible to create a moral atmosphere in which advocacy of violence and terror withers away," she said.

Ross, who brought Israeli, Palestinian and U.S. security experts together during his mission, flew to the region at the weekend after the market bombing threatened to shatter already fragile Israeli-Palestinian ties.
